title: Pydantic is STILL all you need: Jason Liu
talk_summary: Jason Liu argues that structured outputs via Pydantic/Instructor (response_model + validators + retry) should replace free-text JSON parsing for all LLM calls, including RAG, extraction, and agents. The key mechanisms are schema-typed responses, validators that encode 'what correct looks like', and feeding validation error messages back to the model for one retry.

takeaways.technique: Schema-typed LLM outputs with validators and retry-on-validation-error
takeaways.what_they_do: Every LLM call declares a Pydantic response_model; validators encode domain invariants (e.g. price*qty == total, URLs return 200) and on failure the error message is appended to the prompt and the call retried once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I want to I can turn retrying on and that error message is caught by the language model and then used to correct the outputs
takeaways.numbers: one retry is 'basically enough' for OpenAI/Anthropic; 4-5% failure modes on complex validations dropped to ~0 after fine-tuning function calling

takeaways.technique: Programmatic validators as a second gate on LLM review output
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of trusting the model's self-score, validators run real checks (regex URL extraction + HTTP 200 probe) and reject outputs that fail, forcing the model to drop or fix them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I just have a regular expression parse all the URLs and I use po post to figure out if the URL returns a 200 and now I can make sure very easily that no URLs are you know hallucinated

takeaways.technique: Generate a workflow/DAG as structured output instead of a ReAct loop
takeaways.what_they_do: For agentic tasks, have the model emit a typed workflow/DAG object that is handed to a deterministic execution engine, rather than looping ReAct until it hopefully terminates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A lot of it now becomes generating workflows and dags to then go send to an execution engine to do the computation ourselves rather than having some kind of react Loop and hope that these things terminate

takeaways.technique: Structured search-query objects for retrieval (multi-query, parallel)
takeaways.what_they_do: Model emits a Search object (query, date range, limit, source/backend) or an iterable of them; app runs parallel searches and feeds results to an answer step — two functions, two models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can do two parallel search queries collect them together and continue on and so this means that you can build a fairly sophisticated rag application in two functions and two models

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune small/cheap models on function-calling to eliminate validation failures
takeaways.what_they_do: When complex validators show 4-5% failure, fine-tune on function-calling examples to drive failures to zero even on small models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we see like four to five% failure modes and very complex validations but just by fine-tuning language models on function calling we can get them down to zero

takeaways.technique: Streaming iterables/partials to cut latency and enable early validation
takeaways.what_they_do: Use create_iterable/partial so each validated object is emitted as it completes, allowing parallel downstream work and early rendering without hand-rolled JSON parsing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as you set stream equals true you're going to get each object as they return and this is kind of a way of using streaming to improve the latency
